CHAPTER 16 — गीतामृतम् (GITAMRITAM)

Introduction — गीता किम्?

The word गीतामृतम् (Gitamritam) joins गीता (the Song) with अमृतम् (nectar, the drink of immortality): it means 'the nectar of the Gita'. The श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता ('the sacred Song of the Lord') is a dialogue of seven hundred verses set within the great epic महाभारत, in the भीष्मपर्व. On the battlefield of कुरुक्षेत्र, the warrior अर्जुन (Arjuna) is overcome with grief and confusion (विषाद): should he fight a war against his own kinsmen and teachers? His charioteer and friend, भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण (Sri Krishna), answers his doubt not with a single command but with a whole teaching on duty (कर्तव्य), action (कर्म), knowledge (ज्ञान), devotion (भक्ति) and the nature of the self (आत्मन्). Because these verses have consoled and guided people for more than two thousand years, they are rightly called नेक्टर — अमृतम् — for the mind. In this lesson (NIOS Secondary Sanskrit, Course 209) we drink a few drops of that nectar: we read six famous, public-domain श्लोकs of the Gita, learn their शब्दार्थ (word meanings), translate them into simple English, draw out their message (सन्देशः), and use them to learn a little Sanskrit grammar (व्याकरणम्).

Why the Gita matters (गीतायाः महत्त्वम्)

The Gita is loved because it speaks to a problem every human being faces: how should I act, when my duty is hard and its results are uncertain? Its central teaching is कर्मयोग — the yoga of action performed as duty, without selfish craving for its fruit (निष्काम कर्म). It teaches the ideal of the स्थितप्रज्ञ, the person of steady wisdom who is neither shaken by sorrow nor swept away by pleasure. It describes how the divine repeatedly enters the world (अवतार) whenever righteousness (धर्म) declines. And it ends with a message of complete self-surrender (शरणागति). The verses are short, rhythmic and easy to memorise, so that — like a good सुभाषितम् — they teach both language and life at once. Krishna himself calls this knowledge 'राजविद्या राजगुह्यम्', the king of sciences and the king of secrets.

Six verses of the Gita (शब्दार्थ सहित)

1) कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
   मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥ (गीता 2.47)
   शब्दार्थ: कर्मणि = in action, in (doing your) work; एव = only, alone; अधिकारः = right, entitlement; ते = your; मा = not, never; फलेषु = in the fruits (results); कदाचन = ever, at any time; कर्मफलहेतुः = the cause of (motive for) the fruit of action; भूः (मा भूः) = do not become; सङ्गः = attachment, clinging; अस्तु = let there be; अकर्मणि = in inaction, in not doing.
   Translation: Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit of action be your motive, and let there be no attachment in you to inaction.
   सन्देशः (Message): This is the most famous verse of the Gita. Do your duty with your whole heart, but do not be anxious about the reward. Neither work for the fruit alone, nor abandon work out of the fear that the fruit is uncertain. This is निष्काम कर्म — desireless action.

2) योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय ।
   सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥ (गीता 2.48)
   शब्दार्थ: योगस्थः = established in yoga (steady, balanced); कुरु = do, perform (imperative); कर्माणि = actions (object, plural); सङ्गम् = attachment (object); त्यक्त्वा = having given up, abandoning; धनञ्जय = O Dhananjaya (a name of Arjuna, 'winner of wealth'); सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः = in success and failure; समः = equal, even; भूत्वा = having become; समत्वम् = evenness, equanimity; योगः = yoga; उच्यते = is called (passive).
   Translation: Established in yoga, O Dhananjaya, perform your actions, giving up attachment and remaining even-minded in success and failure; this evenness of mind is called yoga.
   सन्देशः (Message): Krishna gives a working definition — समत्वं योगः, 'yoga is equanimity'. To keep the same calm mind whether one succeeds or fails is itself the highest yoga. Effort is ours; the outcome we accept with a steady heart.

3) दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः ।
   वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥ (गीता 2.56)
   शब्दार्थ: दुःखेषु = in sorrows; अनुद्विग्नमनाः = one whose mind is not agitated; सुखेषु = in pleasures; विगतस्पृहः = free from craving (whose longing has departed); वीतरागभयक्रोधः = free from attachment, fear and anger; स्थितधीः = of steady intellect; मुनिः = a sage; उच्यते = is called.
   Translation: One whose mind is unshaken in sorrows, who is free from craving amid pleasures, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger — such a person of steady wisdom is called a sage (a स्थितप्रज्ञ).
   सन्देशः (Message): This is the portrait of the स्थितप्रज्ञ, the ideal of steady wisdom. The sage is not one who has no feelings, but one who is not swept away by them — calm in pain, unattached in pleasure, free of fear and anger.

4) यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत ।
   अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥ (गीता 4.7)
   शब्दार्थ: यदा यदा = whenever; हि = indeed; धर्मस्य = of righteousness, of dharma; ग्लानिः = decline, decay; भवति = happens, comes to be; भारत = O descendant of Bharata (Arjuna); अभ्युत्थानम् = rise, uprising; अधर्मस्य = of unrighteousness; तदा = then; आत्मानम् = myself; सृजामि = I create, I manifest; अहम् = I.
   Translation: Whenever there is a decline of righteousness (dharma), O Bharata, and a rise of unrighteousness (adharma), then I manifest Myself (I take birth).
   सन्देशः (Message): This is the classic statement of the doctrine of अवतार (divine descent). Whenever dharma weakens and adharma grows strong, the divine enters the world to restore the balance. It gives hope that goodness is never finally defeated.

5) परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् ।
   धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥ (गीता 4.8)
   शब्दार्थ: परित्राणाय = for the protection (of); साधूनाम् = of the good/virtuous people; विनाशाय = for the destruction (of); च = and; दुष्कृताम् = of the evil-doers; धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय = for the purpose of re-establishing dharma; सम्भवामि = I am born, I come into being; युगे युगे = in age after age.
   Translation: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of the evil-doers, and for the firm establishment of dharma, I am born in age after age.
   सन्देशः (Message): This verse completes the previous one. The purpose of the divine descent is threefold — to protect the good, to check the wicked, and to re-establish righteousness. It is a promise repeated 'युगे युगे', in every age.

6) सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।
   अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥ (गीता 18.66)
   शब्दार्थ: सर्वधर्मान् = all duties/religions (object, plural); परित्यज्य = giving up completely, abandoning; माम् = to me; एकम् = one, alone; शरणम् = refuge, shelter; व्रज = go, come (imperative); अहम् = I; त्वा = you (accusative); सर्वपापेभ्यः = from all sins (ablative, plural); मोक्षयिष्यामि = I shall liberate; मा शुचः = do not grieve.
   Translation: Abandoning all (other) duties, take refuge in Me alone; I shall liberate you from all sins — do not grieve.
   सन्देशः (Message): This is called the चरमश्लोक, the 'final verse' of the Gita's teaching — its message of complete surrender (शरणागति). When one offers oneself fully to the divine and does one's duty, one need not be afraid; 'मा शुचः', do not grieve, are among the most comforting words in all of Sanskrit.

Two more famous lines to remember

• श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् (गीता 3.35) — 'One's own duty (स्वधर्म), though imperfect, is better than another's duty well performed.' Be true to your own path.
• आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः (गीता 6.5) — 'The self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.' We rise or fall by our own effort.

व्याकरणम् — A little grammar from the verses (English explanation, Devanagari examples)

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — the joining of sounds). When two sounds meet in Sanskrit, they combine and change. Several kinds appear in these verses:
  • यण्-सन्धि (a short इ/उ before a dissimilar vowel becomes य्/व्): कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव (इ + ए → य्+ए); सृजामि + अहम् = सृजाम्यहम् (इ + अ → य्+अ); अस्तु + अकर्मणि = अस्त्वकर्मणि (उ + अ → व्+अ).
  • दीर्घ-सन्धि (short vowel + like vowel = one long vowel): एव + अधिकारः = एवाधिकारः (अ + अ = आ).
  • गुण/विसर्ग-सन्धि: सङ्गः + अस्तु = सङ्गोऽस्तु (अः + अ → ओ + ऽ, the avagraha ऽ marking the lost अ); स्थितधीः + मुनिः = स्थितधीर्मुनिः (visarga ः → र् before म्); अधिकारः + ते = अधिकारस्ते (visarga ः → स् before त).
  • व्यञ्जन-सन्धि (consonant change): तत् + आत्मानम् = तदात्मानम् (त् softens to द् before a vowel).
Splitting a joined form back into its parts (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is a key reading skill: सृजाम्यहम् = सृजामि + अहम्.

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). Sanskrit nouns change their ending to show their role. Examples from the verses (using देव, an a-stem masculine, as a mental model):
  • प्रथमा (nominative, subject): अहम् 'I', मुनिः 'a sage', स्थितधीः 'the steady-minded one'.
  • द्वितीया (accusative, object): कर्माणि 'actions' (object of कुरु), सङ्गम् 'attachment', सर्वधर्मान् 'all duties', आत्मानम् 'myself'.
  • पञ्चमी (ablative, 'from'): सर्वपापेभ्यः 'from all sins' (plural).
  • षष्ठी (genitive, 'of'): धर्मस्य 'of dharma', अधर्मस्य 'of adharma', साधूनाम् 'of the good', दुष्कृताम् 'of the wicked'.
  • सप्तमी (locative, 'in/at'): कर्मणि 'in action', फलेषु 'in the fruits', दुःखेषु 'in sorrows', सुखेषु 'in pleasures', युगे युगे 'in age after age'.
  • चतुर्थी / तादर्थ्य (dative of purpose, 'for'): परित्राणाय 'for protection', विनाशाय 'for destruction', धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय 'for the establishing of dharma'.

(C) शब्दरूप (declension of a noun — worked example). The neuter a-stem फल ('fruit', which appears as फलेषु in verse 1) declines in the प्रथमा (nominative) as: एकवचन फलम् (one), द्विवचन फले (two), बहुवचन फलानि (many). Its सप्तमी बहुवचन (locative plural) is फलेषु — 'in the fruits'. Similarly दुःखेषु and सुखेषु are locative plurals of दुःख and सुख.

(D) धातुरूप (verb conjugation — worked example). Many verbs here are in the लट् लकार (present tense) or the लोट् लकार (imperative). Take the root √भू ('to be/become'), which gives भवति in verse 4. Its लट् लकार (present, परस्मैपद) runs: भवति / भवतः / भवन्ति (he/they), भवसि / भवथः / भवथ (you), भवामि / भवावः / भवामः (I/we). The imperative (लोट्) forms कुरु ('do!', verse 2) and व्रज ('go!', verse 6) are commands addressed to Arjuna. उच्यते ('is called', verses 2 and 3) is a passive (कर्मवाच्य) form, and सृजामि / सम्भवामि / मोक्षयिष्यामि are first-person forms spoken by Krishna ('I create / I am born / I shall liberate').

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you tasted a few drops of the गीतामृतम्, the nectar of the श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता — the dialogue of अर्जुन and भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण on the field of कुरुक्षेत्र. You read six famous public-domain verses: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते (do your duty, not for the fruit), योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि (act with equanimity — समत्वं योगः), दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः (the portrait of the स्थितप्रज्ञ, the sage of steady wisdom), यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य and परित्राणाय साधूनाम् (the doctrine of अवतार — the divine descends to restore dharma), and सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य (the message of complete surrender, शरणागति). For each you studied the शब्दार्थ, an English translation and the सन्देश (message). Finally you drew grammar from the verses: यण्, दीर्घ, गुण, विसर्ग and व्यञ्जन सन्धि (and how to split them), the common विभक्ति endings with examples, a शब्दरूप model (फलम् / फले / फलानि) and a धातुरूप model (भवति; the imperatives कुरु and व्रज). Memorise a verse or two — they will enrich both your Sanskrit and your understanding of life.

topics.name: The Bhagavad Gita — Setting and Significance
topics.description: What the श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता is: a 700-verse dialogue of अर्जुन and श्रीकृष्ण within the महाभारत on the field of कुरुक्षेत्र; why it is called गीतामृतम् (the nectar of the Gita) and why its teaching on duty and the self has guided people for centuries.

topics.name: कर्मयोग — The Yoga of Action (Nishkama Karma)
topics.description: The Gita's central teaching of कर्मयोग through कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते (2.47) and योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि (2.48): doing one's duty without craving for the fruit (निष्काम कर्म), and equanimity in success and failure — समत्वं योगः.

topics.description: The ideal of the स्थितप्रज्ञ from दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः (2.56): the sage unshaken in sorrow, free from craving in pleasure, and free from attachment, fear and anger — steadiness of mind (स्थितधीः) as the goal of yoga.

topics.name: धर्म, Divine Descent (अवतार) and Surrender (शरणागति)
topics.description: The teaching on dharma and अवतार through यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य (4.7) and परित्राणाय साधूनाम् (4.8) — the divine descends to protect the good and restore righteousness — and the message of complete surrender in सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य (18.66).

topics.name: शब्दार्थ — Word Meanings and Vocabulary
topics.description: Building Sanskrit vocabulary through word-by-word शब्दार्थ of the verses: कर्म, फल, सङ्ग, योगस्थ, समत्व, स्थितधी, ग्लानि, अवतार, शरणम्, मोक्षयिष्यामि and other key words, with their English meanings and case-forms.

topics.name: व्याकरणम् and Translation — Grammar and Comprehension
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the verses: यण्/दीर्घ/गुण/विसर्ग/व्यञ्जन सन्धि with सन्धि-विच्छेद, the common विभक्ति case endings, a शब्दरूप model (फलम्) and a धातुरूप model (भू); plus translating verses into simple English and answering comprehension questions.

sections.heading: The Gita — what it is and why it matters
bullets: The श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता is a 700-verse dialogue within the महाभारत in which श्रीकृष्ण answers अर्जुन's doubt and grief (विषाद) on the battlefield of कुरुक्षेत्र.
गीतामृतम् = गीता (Song) + अमृतम् (nectar); the verses are called 'nectar' because they have consoled and guided people for over two thousand years.
Being short and rhythmic, the verses are easy to memorise and teach both Sanskrit and life; Krishna calls this knowledge राजविद्या राजगुह्यम्.

sections.heading: कर्मयोग — duty without craving the fruit
bullets: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन (2.47): your right is to action alone, never to its fruits — do your duty, do not be anxious for the reward.
This is निष्काम कर्म (desireless action): neither work only for the fruit nor abandon work out of fear.
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि... समत्वं योग उच्यते (2.48): act while established in yoga, even-minded in success and failure — equanimity itself is yoga.

sections.heading: स्थितप्रज्ञ — the sage of steady wisdom
bullets: दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः (2.56): the sage's mind is unshaken in sorrow and free of craving in pleasure.
वीतरागभयक्रोधः: he is free from attachment (राग), fear (भय) and anger (क्रोध).
Such a person of steady intellect (स्थितधीः) is called a मुनि — a स्थितप्रज्ञ; not one without feeling, but one not swept away by feeling.

sections.heading: धर्म, अवतार and शरणागति
bullets: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति... तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् (4.7): whenever dharma declines and adharma rises, the divine manifests itself.
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्... सम्भवामि युगे युगे (4.8): the descent is to protect the good, check the wicked and re-establish dharma, age after age.
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज... मा शुचः (18.66): the चरमश्लोक — surrender fully, and 'do not grieve'.

sections.heading: Grammar from the verses
bullets: यण्-सन्धि: कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव; सृजामि + अहम् = सृजाम्यहम्; अस्तु + अकर्मणि = अस्त्वकर्मणि.
विसर्ग/व्यञ्जन-सन्धि: स्थितधीः + मुनिः = स्थितधीर्मुनिः; तत् + आत्मानम् = तदात्मानम्; सङ्गः + अस्तु = सङ्गोऽस्तु.
विभक्ति: फलेषु/दुःखेषु सप्तमी 'in'; सर्वपापेभ्यः पञ्चमी 'from'; धर्मस्य/साधूनाम् षष्ठी 'of'; परित्राणाय/विनाशाय dative 'for'.
शब्दरूप फल (neuter): फलम् / फले / फलानि; धातुरूप भू (present): भवति; imperatives कुरु ('do'), व्रज ('go').

key_takeaways: The श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता is a 700-verse dialogue of अर्जुन and श्रीकृष्ण in the महाभारत; गीतामृतम् means 'the nectar of the Gita'.
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन — do your duty without craving its fruit (निष्काम कर्म).
समत्वं योग उच्यते — keeping an even mind in success and failure is itself yoga.
The स्थितप्रज्ञ is unshaken in sorrow, unattached in pleasure and free of attachment, fear and anger (2.56).
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिः... — whenever dharma declines the divine descends (अवतार) to protect the good and restore righteousness, युगे युगे.
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज... मा शुचः — the message of surrender: give yourself fully, and do not grieve.
यण्-सन्धि turns इ/उ before another vowel into य्/व् (कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव); splitting a sandhi is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

glossary.definition: 'The nectar of the Gita' (गीता + अमृतम्); the title of this selection of श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता verses.
The 700-verse 'Song of the Lord', a dialogue of अर्जुन and श्रीकृष्ण set within the महाभारत on the field of कुरुक्षेत्र.
The yoga of action — performing one's duty as an offering, without selfish attachment to its results.
Desireless action; doing one's duty without craving for its fruit (फल), the teaching of कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते.
Fruit or result of action; the verse warns मा फलेषु कदाचन — never (crave) the fruits.
Evenness or equanimity of mind; समत्वं योग उच्यते — 'equanimity is called yoga' (2.48).
One of steady wisdom; the sage whose mind is unshaken in sorrow and pleasure (2.56), also called स्थितधीः.
Free from attachment (राग), fear (भय) and anger (क्रोध); a quality of the स्थितप्रज्ञ.
Righteousness, duty, the moral order; its decline (ग्लानि) prompts the divine descent.
The 'descent' of the divine into the world, described in यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य... सम्भवामि युगे युगे.
Complete self-surrender to the divine; the message of सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज (18.66).

The joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; e.g. यण्-सन्धि turns इ/उ before a vowel into य्/व्.
A noun's case ending showing its role: प्रथमा subject, द्वितीया object, पञ्चमी 'from', षष्ठी 'of', सप्तमी 'in', dative 'for'.
The conjugation of a verb root through persons and numbers, e.g. √भू present भवति / भवतः / भवन्ति.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — गीतामृतम् (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 16)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the verses in the lesson where needed.

questions.question:
Translate the following verse into simple English:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
questions.answer: Your right is to action (कर्म) alone, never to its fruits (फल). Do not let the fruit of action be your motive, and do not be attached to inaction (अकर्म) either. In short: do your duty wholeheartedly without craving the reward, and do not give up work.
questions.explanation: The famous 2.47 verse on निष्काम कर्म — desireless action.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: कर्मणि, फलेषु, सङ्गः, कदाचन, अधिकारः.
questions.answer: कर्मणि = in action / in work; फलेषु = in the fruits (results); सङ्गः = attachment; कदाचन = ever / at any time; अधिकारः = right, entitlement.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from verse 2.47.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain the meaning of 'समत्वं योग उच्यते'.
questions.answer: It means 'equanimity (evenness of mind) is called yoga'. Keeping the same calm, balanced mind in both success and failure — remaining undisturbed by results — is itself the highest yoga.
questions.explanation: The definition of yoga given in verse 2.48.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) सृजाम्यहम् (b) स्थितधीर्मुनिः.
questions.answer: (a) सृजाम्यहम् = सृजामि + अहम् (इ + अ → य्, यण्-सन्धि). (b) स्थितधीर्मुनिः = स्थितधीः + मुनिः (visarga ः → र् before म्).
questions.explanation: Splitting joined forms is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its meaning-role for each word: फलेषु, धर्मस्य, सर्वपापेभ्यः.
questions.answer: फलेषु = सप्तमी (locative), plural → 'in the fruits'. धर्मस्य = षष्ठी (genitive), singular → 'of dharma'. सर्वपापेभ्यः = पञ्चमी (ablative), plural → 'from all sins'.
questions.explanation: सप्तमी shows place, षष्ठी possession, पञ्चमी source.

questions.question: Explain the doctrine of अवतार using the verses 'यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत, अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम्' and 'परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्, धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे'. Why does this teaching give hope?
questions.answer:
In these verses (Gita 4.7-4.8) Krishna states the doctrine of अवतार, the divine descent. He says: whenever there is a decline (ग्लानि) of righteousness (धर्म) and a rise (अभ्युत्थान) of unrighteousness (अधर्म), then he manifests himself (आत्मानं सृजामि). The purpose is threefold — परित्राणाय साधूनाम् (to protect the good), विनाशाय दुष्कृताम् (to destroy/check the wicked), and धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय (to re-establish dharma) — and this happens युगे युगे, in age after age.
This teaching gives hope because it promises that goodness is never finally defeated. However strong adharma may seem, the divine order responds and dharma is restored. It encourages people to stand on the side of righteousness, trusting that righteousness will ultimately prevail.
questions.explanation: Explains ग्लानि/अभ्युत्थान, the threefold purpose, and युगे युगे; then the message of hope.

questions.question: Describe the qualities of the स्थितप्रज्ञ (the person of steady wisdom) as taught in 'दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः, वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते'. How can a student practise these qualities?
questions.answer:
The verse (Gita 2.56) paints the portrait of the स्थितप्रज्ञ. Such a person is दुःखेषु अनुद्विग्नमनाः — his mind is not agitated in sorrows; सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः — he is free from craving amid pleasures; and वीतरागभयक्रोधः — he is free from attachment (राग), fear (भय) and anger (क्रोध). One of such steady intellect (स्थितधीः) is called a सage (मुनि). The idea is not to have no feelings, but not to be swept away by them.
A student can practise this by staying calm when results are bad and not becoming proud when they are good, by not being greedy for comforts, by controlling anger and fear before exams, and by keeping a balanced, steady mind in both praise and blame.
questions.explanation: Lists the qualities (अनुद्विग्न, विगतस्पृह, वीतरागभयक्रोध) and gives practical application.

questions.question: Translate: 'सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज' and state its message.
questions.answer: Translation: 'Abandoning all (other) duties, take refuge in Me alone.' Message: it teaches शरणागति — complete self-surrender. One who offers oneself fully to the divine and does one's duty need not fear, for the following line promises liberation from all sins and says 'मा शुचः' — do not grieve.
questions.explanation: The चरमश्लोक (18.66) and its message of surrender.

questions.question: What is the श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता, and why is this selection called गीतामृतम्?
questions.answer: The श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता is a dialogue of about 700 verses within the महाभारत, spoken by भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण to अर्जुन on the battlefield of कुरुक्षेत्र, teaching about duty, action, knowledge and devotion. This selection is called गीतामृतम् — 'the nectar (अमृत) of the Gita' — because its verses, like nectar, nourish and console the mind and have guided people for centuries.
questions.explanation: Definition of the Gita plus the meaning of गीतामृतम्.

questions.question: Read: 'योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय'. Who is धनञ्जय, and what is he being asked to do?
questions.answer: धनञ्जय ('winner of wealth') is a name of अर्जुन. He is being asked to perform his actions (कुरु कर्माणि) while established in yoga (योगस्थः) and having given up attachment (सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा) — that is, to do his duty with a steady, unattached mind.
questions.explanation: Identifies धनञ्जय = Arjuna and the instruction to act without attachment.

questions.question: The word 'गीतामृतम्' is made of गीता + ____.

questions.question: What does the word 'गीतामृतम्' mean, and to which text does it refer?

questions.explanation: Word-meaning plus the source text.

questions.question: Where and between whom is the Bhagavad Gita spoken?
questions.answer: The Gita is spoken on the battlefield of कुरुक्षेत्र, within the महाभारत. It is a dialogue between the warrior अर्जुन, who is filled with doubt and grief, and भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण, his charioteer and guide.
questions.explanation: Setting (कुरुक्षेत्र, महाभारत) and speakers.

questions.question: Write the first line of the most famous कर्मयोग verse (2.47) in Devanagari.
questions.explanation: Recall of the opening line of Gita 2.47.

questions.question: In verse 2.48, what is Arjuna asked to give up, and what should he become equal in?
questions.answer: He is asked to give up attachment (सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा) and to become equal-minded (समः) in success and failure (सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः). In short, he should act while established in yoga, unattached and even-minded.
questions.explanation: सङ्ग-त्याग and equanimity in सिद्धि/असिद्धि.

questions.question: Explain the idea of निष्काम कर्म (desireless action) as taught in verse 2.47.
questions.answer: निष्काम कर्म means performing one's duty without selfish craving for its fruit. Verse 2.47 says our right (अधिकार) is only to action (कर्म), never to its results (फल). So we should do our duty wholeheartedly, but neither work merely for the reward nor be the 'cause of the fruit' in our own mind. At the same time, we must not be attached to inaction (अकर्म) — that is, we should not give up work either. Effort is in our hands; the outcome we accept calmly.
questions.explanation: Duty without craving the fruit; not abandoning work.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: कर्मणि, फलेषु, अधिकारः.
questions.answer: कर्मणि = in action / in work; फलेषु = in the fruits (results); अधिकारः = right, entitlement.
questions.explanation: Word meanings from verse 2.47.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: राग, भय, क्रोध.
questions.answer: राग = attachment; भय = fear; क्रोध = anger. (The स्थितप्रज्ञ is वीतराग-भय-क्रोधः, free from all three.)
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from verse 2.56.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: ग्लानिः, साधूनाम्, दुष्कृताम्.
questions.answer: ग्लानिः = decline/decay; साधूनाम् = of the good/virtuous; दुष्कृताम् = of the evil-doers.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from verses 4.7-4.8.

questions.question: State and briefly explain three qualities of the स्थितप्रज्ञ from verse 2.56.
questions.answer: From verse 2.56, three qualities are: (1) दुःखेषु अनुद्विग्नमनाः — the mind is not agitated in sorrows; (2) सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः — free from craving amid pleasures; (3) वीतरागभयक्रोधः — free from attachment (राग), fear (भय) and anger (क्रोध). Such a person of steady intellect (स्थितधीः) stays calm and balanced in all situations.
questions.explanation: Three qualities: unshaken, uncraving, free of राग/भय/क्रोध.

questions.question: Does being a स्थितप्रज्ञ mean having no feelings? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: No. The स्थितप्रज्ञ is not a person without feelings. Rather, he is one who is not swept away by his feelings — he stays calm in sorrow, does not crave in pleasure, and controls fear and anger. The point is steadiness and mastery of the mind, not the absence of emotion.
questions.explanation: Steadiness, not feelinglessness.

questions.question: According to verses 4.7-4.8, when and why does the divine descend (अवतार)?
questions.answer: According to 4.7, whenever there is a decline (ग्लानि) of dharma and a rise (अभ्युत्थान) of adharma, the divine manifests itself. According to 4.8, the purpose is threefold: परित्राणाय साधूनाम् (to protect the good), विनाशाय दुष्कृताम् (to destroy/check the wicked), and धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय (to re-establish dharma). This happens युगे युगे, in age after age.
questions.explanation: When: dharma declines; Why: protect good, check wicked, restore dharma.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि'.
questions.answer: 'Established in yoga, perform your actions.' योगस्थः = established in yoga; कुरु = perform; कर्माणि = actions.
questions.explanation: Simple translation of the opening of 2.48.

questions.question: Translate the full verse 'दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः, वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते'.
questions.answer: One whose mind is unshaken (अनुद्विग्नमनाः) in sorrows (दुःखेषु), who is free from craving (विगतस्पृहः) amid pleasures (सुखेषु), and who is free from attachment, fear and anger (वीतरागभयक्रोधः) — such a person of steady wisdom (स्थितधीः) is called a sage (मुनि).
questions.explanation: Full translation of Gita 2.56.

questions.question: Translate 'यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत' and name the doctrine it states.
questions.answer: 'Whenever there is a decline of dharma (righteousness), O Bharata...' It begins the statement of the doctrine of अवतार — the divine descent that occurs whenever dharma declines and adharma rises.
questions.explanation: Translation + names the अवतार doctrine.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of: (a) कर्मण्येव (b) तदात्मानम्.
questions.answer: (a) कर्मण्येव = कर्मणि + एव (इ + ए → य्, यण्-सन्धि). (b) तदात्मानम् = तत् + आत्मानम् (त् → द् before a vowel, व्यञ्जन-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting joined forms.

questions.question: Join by sandhi: (a) सृजामि + अहम् (b) स्थितधीः + मुनिः.
questions.answer: (a) सृजामि + अहम् = सृजाम्यहम् (इ + अ → य्, यण्-सन्धि). (b) स्थितधीः + मुनिः = स्थितधीर्मुनिः (visarga ः → र् before म्).
questions.explanation: यण्-सन्धि and विसर्ग-सन्धि joins.

questions.answer: प्रथमा: एकवचन फलम्, द्विवचन फले, बहुवचन फलानि.
questions.explanation: Declension of neuter a-stem फल, nominative.

questions.question: Which verse would you quote to a friend who is very anxious about an exam result, and why?
questions.answer: I would quote 'कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन'. It teaches that our right is to effort (action), not to the result, so one should study sincerely but not be anxious about the outcome — do your duty and keep a calm mind.
questions.explanation: Applies निष्काम कर्म to exam anxiety.

questions.question: By which name is Arjuna addressed in verse 2.48, and what does it mean?
questions.answer: He is addressed as धनञ्जय, which means 'winner of wealth' — a well-known name of Arjuna, given because he won great wealth for the kingdom.
questions.explanation: धनञ्जय = 'winner of wealth', a name of Arjuna.

questions.question: 'Wrongdoers seem powerful today, so goodness has no chance.' Using verses 4.7-4.8, respond to this view.
questions.answer: The verses reply that goodness is never finally defeated. Krishna says that whenever dharma declines (ग्लानि) and adharma rises, he manifests himself (4.7) for the protection of the good, the checking of the wicked, and the re-establishment of dharma — and that this happens युगे युगे, in every age (4.8). So however strong wrongdoers may seem, the moral order responds and righteousness is restored. This gives us hope and encourages us to stand firmly on the side of dharma.
questions.explanation: Applies the अवतार doctrine to answer despair.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: त्यक्त्वा, योगस्थः, समत्वम्.
questions.answer: त्यक्त्वा = having given up/abandoned; योगस्थः = established/steady in yoga; समत्वम् = evenness/equanimity.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from verse 2.48.

questions.question: Translate 'सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि' into English.
questions.answer: 'I shall liberate (you) from all sins.' सर्वपापेभ्यः = from all sins (ablative plural); मोक्षयिष्यामि = I shall liberate/free.
questions.explanation: Translation of part of verse 18.66.

questions.question: What is the श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता? Explain its setting, its speakers and why it is treasured.
questions.answer:
The श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता ('the sacred Song of the Lord') is a dialogue of about 700 verses that forms part of the great epic महाभारत. Its setting is the battlefield of कुरुक्षेत्र, just before a great war. The warrior अर्जुन, overcome with grief and doubt about fighting his own kinsmen, turns to his charioteer and friend भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण for guidance. Krishna's answer is the Gita.
The Gita is treasured for several reasons: (1) it addresses a problem every person faces — how to act rightly when duty is hard and results uncertain; (2) it teaches कर्मयोग (desireless action), the ideal of the स्थितप्रज्ञ, the doctrine of अवतार, and the peace of surrender; (3) its verses are short, rhythmic and easy to memorise, teaching both Sanskrit and life; and (4) they have consoled and guided people for over two thousand years, which is why this selection is called गीतामृतम्, 'the nectar of the Gita'.
questions.explanation: Definition, setting, speakers and fourfold value.

questions.question: Take the verse 'कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन, मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि'. Give its word meanings and full explanation.
questions.answer:
शब्दार्थ: कर्मणि = in action; एव = alone; अधिकारः = right; ते = your; मा = never; फलेषु = in the fruits; कदाचन = ever; कर्मफलहेतुः = cause of the fruit of action; मा भूः = do not become; सङ्गः = attachment; अस्तु = let there be; अकर्मणि = in inaction.
Explanation: This is the Gita's most famous verse, the heart of कर्मयोग. It gives four instructions. (1) Your right is to action alone — you can control your effort, your duty. (2) But never to its fruits — the result is not fully in your hands, so do not make it your obsession. (3) Do not let the desire for the fruit be the sole motive of your action. (4) Yet do not become attached to inaction either — do not give up your duty out of fear that the result is uncertain. The verse thus teaches निष्काम कर्म: work sincerely and fully, offer the effort, and accept the result with a calm mind.
questions.explanation: Word meanings + the four-part teaching of निष्काम कर्म.

questions.question: Discuss the message of surrender (शरणागति) in 'सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज, अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः', and explain why it is called the चरमश्लोक.
questions.answer:
This verse (Gita 18.66) is the Gita's final and most reassuring teaching. Krishna says: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य — giving up (dependence on) all other duties; मामेकं शरणं व्रज — take refuge in Me alone; अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि — I shall liberate you from all sins; मा शुचः — do not grieve. The message is शरणागति, complete self-surrender: when a person offers himself fully to the divine and does his duty with trust, he need not be anxious or afraid.
It is called the चरमश्लोक ('final verse') because it comes near the very end of the Gita and sums up its whole teaching in a single promise of grace and fearlessness. The two words मा शुचः — 'do not grieve' — are among the most comforting in all of Sanskrit, turning Arjuna's grief at the start of the Gita into peace at its close. The verse balances effort (doing one's duty) with faith (surrender), showing that the two are not opposed.
questions.explanation: Explains surrender, the promise of liberation, and why it is the चरमश्लोक.

questions.question: Write any TWO verses from the lesson in Devanagari and state the message of each.
questions.answer:
1. कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन। मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥ — Message: do your duty without craving the fruit (निष्काम कर्म), and do not give up work either.
2. यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत। अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम्॥ — Message: whenever righteousness declines and unrighteousness rises, the divine descends (अवतार) to restore dharma.
questions.explanation: Recall of two verses + their messages.

questions.question: Compare the calm of the स्थितप्रज्ञ (2.56) with the equanimity (समत्व) taught in the कर्मयोग verse 2.48. How are they connected?
questions.answer:
Both verses point to the same steady, balanced state of mind. In 2.48, कर्मयोग asks us to act while 'सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा' — being equal in success and failure — and calls this equanimity (समत्व) itself yoga. In 2.56, the स्थितप्रज्ञ is described as 'दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः' — unshaken in sorrow, free of craving in pleasure — and 'वीतरागभयक्रोधः', free of attachment, fear and anger.
The two are deeply connected: the equanimity that कर्मयोग practises in action is the very calm that the स्थितप्रज्ञ has made his steady nature. In other words, by doing one's duty without craving the fruit (2.48), one gradually becomes the person of steady wisdom (2.56). Action done with समत्व is the path; the स्थितप्रज्ञ is the goal.
questions.explanation: Links समत्व (path) with स्थितप्रज्ञ (goal).

questions.question: Translate the verse 'योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय, सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते' and explain it.
questions.answer:
Translation: 'Established in yoga, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), perform your actions, having given up attachment and remaining equal-minded in success and failure; this evenness of mind is called yoga.'
Explanation: Krishna gives Arjuna a practical working definition of yoga. One should act (कुरु कर्माणि) — duty is not to be abandoned. But the action should be done योगस्थः, from a steady inner state, after giving up attachment (सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा) to results. Whether the effort brings success (सिद्धि) or failure (असिद्धि), one should keep the same calm mind. This very evenness — समत्वम् — is what the Gita means by yoga. The verse thus joins action with inner balance.
questions.explanation: Translation + explanation of समत्वं योगः.

questions.question: Explain सन्धि and सन्धि-विच्छेद with four examples taken from the verses of this chapter.
questions.answer:
सन्धि is the joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; सन्धि-विच्छेद is splitting such a joined form back into its parts. Examples from the verses:
1. कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव (इ + ए → य्, यण्-सन्धि).
2. सृजामि + अहम् = सृजाम्यहम् (इ + अ → य्, यण्-सन्धि).
3. स्थितधीः + मुनिः = स्थितधीर्मुनिः (visarga ः → र् before म्, विसर्ग-सन्धि).
4. तत् + आत्मानम् = तदात्मानम् (त् → द् before a vowel, व्यञ्जन-सन्धि).
Being able to both join (सन्धि) and split (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is essential for reading Gita verses correctly.
questions.explanation: Definition + four worked examples with rules.

questions.question: Identify the विभक्ति (case) of five words from the verses — फलेषु, धर्मस्य, सर्वपापेभ्यः, कर्माणि, परित्राणाय — and give the English sense of each.
questions.answer:
1. फलेषु — सप्तमी (locative), plural: 'in the fruits'.
2. धर्मस्य — षष्ठी (genitive): 'of dharma'.
3. सर्वपापेभ्यः — पञ्चमी (ablative), plural: 'from all sins'.
4. कर्माणि — द्वितीया (accusative), plural: 'actions' (the object of कुरु).
5. परित्राणाय — चतुर्थी / dative of purpose: 'for the protection (of)'.
Recognising these endings tells us the role each word plays in the verse.
questions.explanation: Five cases with senses drawn from the verses.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
(a) To what alone is one's right? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'फलेषु'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'कर्मण्येव'. (d) State the message.
questions.answer: (a) One's right (अधिकार) is to action (कर्म) alone. (b) फलेषु = 'in the fruits (results)'. (c) कर्मण्येव = कर्मणि + एव (यण्-सन्धि). (d) Message: do your duty without craving its fruit (निष्काम कर्म), and do not cling to inaction either.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: meaning, word, sandhi split and message.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते॥
(a) In what state should one perform actions? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'समत्वम्'. (c) In which विभक्ति is 'कर्माणि'? (d) How is yoga defined here?
questions.answer: (a) One should perform actions योगस्थः — established/steady in yoga, having given up attachment. (b) समत्वम् = evenness/equanimity. (c) कर्माणि is द्वितीया (accusative), the object of कुरु. (d) Yoga is defined as समत्व — equanimity in success and failure.
questions.explanation: Comprehension with a case identification.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते॥
(a) How is the sage's mind in sorrows? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'क्रोधः'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'स्थितधीर्मुनिः'. (d) Whom does this verse describe?
questions.answer: (a) In sorrows (दुःखेषु) the sage's mind is unshaken (अनुद्विग्न). (b) क्रोधः = anger. (c) स्थितधीर्मुनिः = स्थितधीः + मुनिः (visarga → र्). (d) It describes the स्थितप्रज्ञ, the person of steady wisdom.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: the स्थितप्रज्ञ, with a sandhi split.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम्॥
(a) When does the divine manifest? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'ग्लानिः'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'तदात्मानम्'. (d) What doctrine does this verse state?
questions.answer: (a) The divine manifests whenever dharma declines and adharma rises. (b) ग्लानिः = decline/decay. (c) तदात्मानम् = तत् + आत्मानम् (त् → द्). (d) It states the doctrine of अवतार (divine descent).
questions.explanation: Comprehension: अवतार doctrine, with a sandhi split.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे॥
(a) For whose protection is the descent? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'दुष्कृताम्'. (c) In which विभक्ति is 'साधूनाम्'? (d) When does this happen?
questions.answer: (a) For the protection of the good/virtuous (साधूनाम्). (b) दुष्कृताम् = of the evil-doers. (c) साधूनाम् is षष्ठी (genitive), plural. (d) It happens युगे युगे — in age after age.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: the threefold purpose of the अवतार.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज।
अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः॥
(a) What is one asked to do? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'शरणम्'. (c) What do the words 'मा शुचः' mean? (d) What is the message of this verse?
questions.answer: (a) One is asked to give up (dependence on) all other duties and take refuge in the divine alone. (b) शरणम् = refuge/shelter. (c) मा शुचः = 'do not grieve'. (d) Message: complete surrender (शरणागति) brings freedom from sin and fear — do not grieve.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: the message of surrender (18.66).

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
(a) In which विभक्ति is 'फलेषु'? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'सङ्गः'. (c) The avagraha (ऽ) in 'सङ्गोऽस्तु' marks a lost ____. (d) What kind of action does the verse teach?
questions.answer: (a) फलेषु is सप्तमी (locative), plural — 'in the fruits'. (b) सङ्गः = attachment. (c) The avagraha ऽ marks a lost अ (सङ्गः + अस्तु = सङ्गोऽस्तु). (d) It teaches निष्काम कर्म — desireless action.
questions.explanation: Comprehension with case and avagraha.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
A student studies hard for a competition. She does her best in the contest but is not overjoyed when she wins nor broken when she loses.
(a) Which Gita verse does her attitude reflect? (b) What is this attitude called in one Sanskrit phrase? (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'समः'. (d) Why is such an attitude helpful?
questions.answer: (a) It reflects 'योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि... समत्वं योग उच्यते' (2.48) and 'कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते' (2.47). (b) It is called समत्व (equanimity) or निष्काम कर्म. (c) समः = equal, even. (d) Such an even mind keeps her calm and steady, free from anxiety and pride, so she can keep improving without being disturbed by results.
questions.explanation: Applies समत्व/निष्काम कर्म to a real situation.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते॥
(a) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'सुखेषु'. (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'भयम्'. (c) In which विभक्ति are 'दुःखेषु' and 'सुखेषु'? (d) What is such a person called?
questions.answer: (a) सुखेषु = 'in pleasures'. (b) भयम् = fear. (c) दुःखेषु and सुखेषु are सप्तमी (locative), plural. (d) Such a person is called a मुनि (sage) — a स्थितप्रज्ञ / स्थितधीः.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary and case comprehension from 2.56.

questions.question:
Read the line and answer:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्। (गीता 3.35)
(a) What is said to be better — one's own duty or another's? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'स्वधर्मः'. (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'श्रेयान्'. (d) What lesson does this line teach?
questions.answer: (a) One's own duty (स्वधर्म) is said to be better, even if imperfect, than another's duty well performed. (b) स्वधर्मः = one's own duty. (c) श्रेयान् = better, more excellent. (d) Lesson: be true to your own path and duty rather than imitating someone else's.
questions.explanation: Comprehension on स्वधर्म (Gita 3.35).
